questions.text: The Extended Fund Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan by the IMF Executive Board in September 2024 was worth approximately how much?
questions.explanation: The IMF Board approved a 37-month Extended Arrangement of SDR 5,320 million, about US$7 billion, on 25 September 2024.

questions.text: What is the duration of the Extended Fund Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan in September 2024?
questions.explanation: The arrangement was approved as a 37-month Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility.

questions.text: Which IMF programme did Pakistan complete immediately before entering the 2024 Extended Fund Facility?
options: A nine-month Stand-By Arrangement of about US$3 billion
A Rapid Financing Instrument of about US$1.4 billion
A Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust loan
A Flexible Credit Line of about US$6 billion
questions.explanation: Pakistan completed a nine-month Stand-By Arrangement of about US$3 billion, approved in July 2023, before the 2024 Extended Fund Facility.

questions.text: In May 2025 the IMF Executive Board approved for Pakistan, alongside the first EFF review, an arrangement under which facility?
questions.explanation: On 9 May 2025 the Board completed the first EFF review and approved a new arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, which finances climate-related reforms.

questions.text: The Resilience and Sustainability Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan in May 2025 was worth approximately how much?
questions.explanation: The RSF arrangement was approved at about US$1.4 billion to support climate-resilience reforms.

questions.text: The IMF disbursement released to Pakistan on completion of the first review of the Extended Fund Facility in May 2025 was approximately how much?
questions.explanation: Completion of the first EFF review on 9 May 2025 allowed an immediate disbursement of about US$1 billion (SDR 760 million).

questions.text: In which month did the IMF Executive Board complete the second review of Pakistan's Extended Fund Facility, unlocking a tranche of about US$1.2 billion?
questions.explanation: The Board completed the second EFF review and the first RSF review on 8 December 2025, releasing about US$1.2 billion.

questions.text: The IMF Executive Board completed the third review of Pakistan's Extended Fund Facility in May 2026, approving a total immediate disbursement of about how much?
questions.explanation: The 8 May 2026 decision released about US$1.1 billion under the EFF and about US$220 million under the RSF, roughly US$1.32 billion in total.

questions.text: After the third EFF review in May 2026, total IMF disbursements to Pakistan under the EFF and RSF arrangements stood at approximately how much?
questions.explanation: Cumulative disbursements under the two arrangements reached about US$4.8 billion (SDR 3,348 million) after the May 2026 decision.

questions.text: What was the total outlay of Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 federal budget carried a total outlay of about Rs17.573 trillion, some 7 percent lower than the previous year's budget.

questions.text: What tax collection target was set for the Federal Board of Revenue in the federal budget for 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 budget set an FBR revenue target of Rs14,131 billion, about 9 percent above the previous year's target.

questions.text: How much was allocated to defence in Pakistan's federal budget for 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Defence was allocated Rs2,550 billion in the FY2025-26 budget, an increase of about 20 percent over the previous year.

questions.text: What real GDP growth target did the government set in the federal budget for 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 budget targeted real GDP growth of 4.2 percent; actual growth came in lower.

questions.text: What inflation target was set for fiscal year 2025-26 in Pakistan's federal budget?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 budget assumed average inflation of 7.5 percent for the year.

questions.text: The federal budget for 2025-26 set the fiscal deficit target at what share of GDP?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 budget targeted a fiscal deficit of 3.9 percent of GDP, down from a 5.9 percent target the previous year.

questions.text: Which new levy on petroleum products was introduced in Pakistan's federal budget for 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 budget imposed a carbon levy of Rs2.50 per litre on petrol, diesel and furnace oil.

questions.text: What pay increase was announced for federal government employees in grades 1 to 20 in the 2025-26 federal budget?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 budget granted a 10 percent pay rise to federal employees in grades 1-20 and a 7 percent increase in pensions.

questions.text: What was the total outlay of Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2026-27?
questions.explanation: The FY2026-27 federal budget carried a total outlay of about Rs18.771 trillion, roughly 7 percent higher than the previous year.

questions.text: Who presented Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2026-27 in the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb presented the FY2026-27 budget in June 2026.

questions.text: In which month was Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27 presented?
questions.explanation: The FY2026-27 budget was presented in June 2026, in line with the usual budget calendar.

questions.text: What FBR tax collection target was set in Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
questions.explanation: The FY2026-27 budget set an FBR target of about Rs15.26 trillion, some 8 percent above the previous year's target.

questions.text: How much was allocated to defence in Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
questions.explanation: Defence spending was set at about Rs3 trillion in the FY2026-27 budget, an increase of roughly 15.6 percent.

questions.text: The federal budget for 2026-27 set the fiscal deficit target at what share of GDP?
questions.explanation: The FY2026-27 budget targeted a fiscal deficit of 3.6 percent of GDP alongside a primary surplus of 2 percent of GDP.

questions.text: To what level was the monthly minimum wage raised in Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
questions.explanation: The FY2026-27 budget raised the minimum wage from Rs37,000 to Rs40,700 per month.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, what was the country's real GDP growth in fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey 2025-26 recorded provisional GDP growth of 3.7 percent, the fastest in four years but short of the 4.2 percent target.

questions.text: Which sector recorded the highest growth rate in Pakistan in fiscal year 2025-26 according to the Economic Survey 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Services grew about 4.09 percent, ahead of industry at about 3.51 percent and agriculture at about 2.89 percent.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, per capita income in FY2025-26 rose to approximately what level?
questions.explanation: Per capita income was reported at about US$1,901 in FY2025-26, up from about US$1,751 the previous year.

questions.text: What poverty rate did the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26 report for the country?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that poverty had risen to 28.9 percent.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, total public debt at the end of March 2026 stood at approximately how much?
questions.explanation: Total public debt was reported at about Rs83,285 billion, roughly Rs83 trillion, at end-March 2026.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, what was Pakistan's real GDP growth in fiscal year 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey 2024-25 put provisional GDP growth for FY2024-25 at 2.68 percent.

questions.text: What were Pakistan's total merchandise exports in fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics data put FY2025-26 exports at about US$30.126 billion, down nearly 6 percent year-on-year.

questions.text: What were Pakistan's total merchandise imports in fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Imports rose about 7.9 percent to roughly US$69.6 billion in FY2025-26.

questions.text: Pakistan's merchandise trade deficit in fiscal year 2025-26 was approximately how large?
questions.explanation: The trade deficit widened by about 21.6 percent to roughly US$39.5 billion in FY2025-26.

questions.text: Workers' remittances to Pakistan in fiscal year 2025-26 reached what record level?
questions.explanation: The State Bank reported record remittances of about US$41.6 billion in FY2025-26, a rise of roughly 8.6 percent.

questions.text: Which country was the largest single source of workers' remittances to Pakistan in fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia sent about US$9.78 billion in FY2025-26, ahead of the UAE at about US$8.81 billion.

questions.text: Pakistan's exports of information technology and IT-enabled services crossed which milestone for the first time in fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: IT and IT-enabled services exports set a record above US$4 billion in FY2025-26, up from about US$3.8 billion the previous year.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, the average rupee-dollar exchange rate in FY2025-26 was approximately what?
questions.explanation: The Survey reported an average exchange rate of about Rs281.1 per US dollar during FY2025-26.

questions.text: What was the State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate after the Monetary Policy Committee decision of April 2026?
questions.explanation: The MPC raised the policy rate by 100 basis points to 11.5 percent in April 2026 and held it there in subsequent meetings.

questions.text: The State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate increase in April 2026 was the first rise in the rate since which year?
questions.explanation: The 100 basis point increase in April 2026 was Pakistan's first policy rate hike since June 2023.

questions.text: What was the peak level of the State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate before the monetary easing cycle that began in June 2024?
questions.explanation: The policy rate peaked at 22 percent, held from June 2023 until the first cut in June 2024.

questions.text: In August 2025 Moody's upgraded Pakistan's sovereign credit rating to which level?
questions.explanation: Moody's raised Pakistan's rating from Caa2 to Caa1 in August 2025, citing an improving external position.

questions.text: In April 2025 Fitch Ratings upgraded Pakistan's long-term sovereign credit rating to which level?
questions.explanation: Fitch upgraded Pakistan from CCC+ to B- with a stable outlook in April 2025, and later affirmed that rating.

questions.text: In July 2026 S&P Global Ratings upgraded Pakistan's long-term sovereign credit rating from B- to which level?
questions.explanation: S&P raised Pakistan's long-term sovereign rating to B with a stable outlook in July 2026, citing stronger institutional capacity for reform.

questions.text: In May 2026 Pakistan issued its first ever Panda bond. In which market and currency was it issued?
options: Hong Kong's offshore market, in US dollars
questions.explanation: A Panda bond is a renminbi-denominated bond sold by a foreign issuer in China's onshore capital market; Pakistan debuted there in May 2026.

questions.text: How much did Pakistan raise through its inaugural Panda bond issued in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Pakistan raised RMB 1.75 billion, about US$250 million, in its debut Panda bond, which was more than five times oversubscribed.

questions.text: In January 2025 the World Bank Group announced a ten-year Country Partnership Framework for Pakistan of approximately what value?
questions.explanation: The World Bank Group announced a Country Partnership Framework for Pakistan worth about US$40 billion over ten years, covering 2026-2035.

questions.text: Which consortium won the bid to acquire a majority stake in Pakistan International Airlines in December 2025?
options: A consortium led by Arif Habib
A consortium led by Fauji Foundation
A consortium led by Serene Air
questions.explanation: An Arif Habib-led consortium won the PIA privatisation bid in December 2025 with an offer of Rs135 billion.

questions.text: What was the winning bid amount for the majority stake in Pakistan International Airlines offered in December 2025?
questions.explanation: The winning consortium bid Rs135 billion for a 75 percent stake, against a government reference price of Rs100 billion.

questions.text: Which mobile operator did Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited acquire under a transaction cleared by the Competition Commission of Pakistan in 2025?
questions.explanation: The Competition Commission of Pakistan approved PTCL's acquisition of Telenor Pakistan in 2025, consolidating the mobile market.

questions.text: The Rs1.225 trillion financing deal that the government signed with commercial banks in 2025 was intended to retire debt in which sector?
questions.explanation: The deal with a consortium of commercial banks was designed to clear a large part of the power sector's circular debt.

questions.text: In April 2025 the Prime Minister announced a reduction in electricity tariffs of approximately how much per unit?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a cut of Rs7.41 per unit in electricity prices in early April 2025.

questions.text: Mainline-1, the railway upgrade project under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, runs between which two cities?
questions.explanation: ML-1 is the roughly 1,700-kilometre Karachi-Peshawar main railway line, the largest infrastructure project under CPEC.

questions.text: In September 2025 Pakistan and China agreed to finance the ML-1 railway project through a consortium including which two multilateral lenders?
questions.explanation: The agreed financing consortium for the roughly US$7 billion ML-1 project included the Asian Development Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank alongside China and Pakistan.

questions.text: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor was formally launched during a visit by the Chinese President in which year?
questions.explanation: CPEC agreements were signed during President Xi Jinping's visit to Pakistan in April 2015.

questions.text: The Reko Diq copper and gold project is located in which district of Balochistan?
questions.explanation: Reko Diq lies in Chagai district in western Balochistan, near the borders with Iran and Afghanistan.

questions.text: Which company holds a 50 percent stake and operates the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Under the 2022 reconstituted arrangement, Barrick holds 50 percent of Reko Diq and operates it, with the remainder split between federal entities and Balochistan.

questions.text: The 34 memoranda of understanding signed between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in October 2024 were valued at approximately how much?
questions.explanation: The October 2024 agreements were reported at a combined value of about US$2.8 billion.

questions.text: In February 2025 Pakistan signed an agreement with Saudi Arabia to defer payment for oil imports worth approximately how much?
questions.explanation: Pakistan signed an agreement in February 2025 for a US$1.2 billion Saudi oil facility on deferred payment terms.

questions.text: In October 2025 Pakistan and Saudi Arabia launched which economic arrangement?
questions.explanation: The two countries launched a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Framework in October 2025 covering trade, investment, energy, mining and IT.

questions.text: At the ECO summit in July 2025 Pakistan signed an investment agreement with which country worth about US$2 billion?
questions.explanation: Pakistan and Azerbaijan signed a US$2 billion investment agreement on the sidelines of the ECO summit in July 2025.

questions.text: Under the trade arrangement announced with the United States in July 2025, Pakistani exports to the US were made subject to a tariff of what rate?
questions.explanation: The July 2025 arrangement set a 19 percent tariff on Pakistani goods entering the United States, lower than the rate initially threatened.

questions.text: Which sector featured prominently in the July 2025 Pakistan-United States trade understanding besides tariff reduction?
questions.explanation: The understanding included cooperation on developing Pakistan's oil and gas reserves alongside the tariff arrangement.

questions.text: In December 2024 the Prime Minister launched which five-year national economic transformation plan?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched 'Uraan Pakistan', the National Economic Transformation Plan 2024-29, on 31 December 2024.

questions.text: The Uraan Pakistan plan launched in December 2024 is built around a framework known by what name?
questions.explanation: Uraan Pakistan is organised around the 5Es: Exports, E-Pakistan, Environment and climate, Energy and infrastructure, and Equity and empowerment.

questions.text: The Uraan Pakistan plan sets a target of raising annual exports to approximately what level by 2029?
questions.explanation: Uraan Pakistan aims to roughly double exports to about US$60 billion a year by 2029.

questions.text: Under the National Tariff Policy 2025-30, the maximum customs duty slab is to be brought down to what rate?
questions.explanation: The policy reduces the tariff structure to four slabs with a maximum rate of 15 percent over five years.

questions.text: Which two import levies is Pakistan's National Tariff Policy 2025-30 designed to phase out entirely?
options: Regulatory duties and additional customs duties
Sales tax and federal excise duty
questions.explanation: The policy commits to eliminating regulatory duties and additional customs duties over about five years.

questions.text: The Special Investment Facilitation Council, created to fast-track foreign investment in Pakistan, was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The Special Investment Facilitation Council was set up in June 2023 to coordinate investment in priority sectors such as minerals, agriculture, IT and energy.

questions.text: The National Fiscal Pact, under which provinces committed to take on additional spending responsibilities and raise agricultural income tax, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The National Fiscal Pact was signed by the federal government and the provinces in September 2024 as part of the IMF programme commitments.

questions.text: The Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, created under legislation passed in 2025, regulates which sector?
questions.explanation: PVARA was established under the 2025 virtual assets law to license and supervise virtual asset service providers.

questions.text: The KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange recorded a gain of approximately what percentage during fiscal year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The KSE-100 rose about 44 percent during FY2025-26, outperforming other domestic asset classes for a third straight year.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, Pakistan's total liquid foreign exchange reserves in mid-May 2026 stood at approximately how much?
questions.explanation: The Survey reported total liquid reserves of about US$22.6 billion on 15 May 2026, of which about US$17.1 billion was held by the State Bank.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, average consumer price inflation during July-April of FY2024-25 fell to approximately what level?
questions.explanation: Average CPI inflation fell to about 4.7 percent during July-April FY2024-25, down from about 26 percent in the same period a year earlier.

questions.text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, average consumer price inflation during July-April of FY2025-26 rose to approximately what level?
questions.explanation: Average CPI inflation was about 6.19 percent during July-April FY2025-26, up from about 4.73 percent a year earlier.

questions.text: The Extended Fund Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan in 2024 was denominated in which unit of account?
questions.explanation: IMF arrangements are denominated in Special Drawing Rights; Pakistan's arrangement was SDR 5,320 million, about US$7 billion.

questions.text: Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2025-26 was presented in which month?
questions.explanation: The FY2025-26 federal budget was presented in June 2025, ahead of the fiscal year beginning on 1 July.

questions.text: Pakistan's fiscal year for budget purposes runs between which dates?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's fiscal year runs from 1 July to 30 June, so FY2025-26 ended on 30 June 2026.

questions.text: Which institution publishes the Pakistan Economic Survey each year on the eve of the federal budget?
questions.explanation: The Pakistan Economic Survey is issued by the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance a day before the budget is presented.

questions.text: Which body in Pakistan takes the decision on the policy interest rate?
options: Monetary Policy Committee of the State Bank of Pakistan
questions.explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee of the State Bank of Pakistan sets the policy rate at its scheduled meetings.

questions.text: Which organisation compiles Pakistan's monthly merchandise trade statistics used to report annual export and import totals?
options: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
questions.explanation: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics publishes the monthly and annual merchandise trade data on which the FY2025-26 figures were based.
